articles.title: Carrie, Avatar, and More of the Most Anticipated Movies and TV Shows to Stream in October
articles.summary: From yet another Mike Flanagan adaptation of a Stephen King story to a Friday the 13th prequel series and the Season 1 finale of Lanterns, here are our picks for what to stream this month.
body: October is finally here to bring spooky season to the world — please ignore the Christmas decorations already on display at your local pharmacy — and that means plenty of terrifying television coming to your screen this month as well!

Don’t worry; it’s not all scares and screams, as we’ve also got some highly anticipated drama debuts, the finale of one of the most discussed superhero series in recent years, the debut of what looks to be one of the other most discussed superhero series in recent years, and much more.
So without further delay, let’s get into our list of 10 picks for movies and TV shows we can’t wait to stream this month. There’s so much good stuff, it’s… scary!

While MCU fans will probably be thrilled to see Black Widow (Florence Pugh) and the new Professor X (Christopher Abbott) play opposite each other, and costume drama aficionados are feasting with this latest sumptuous literary adaptation (John Steinbeck this time), the real story of Netflix’s East of Eden is behind the scenes.

articles.title: 'Lanterns' Makes Even More Sense If You Know About DC's Iconic 20-Year-Old Meme
articles.summary: HBO Max's Lanterns has made the cosmic side of the DC Universe more popular than it's been in a while. Largely due to the adventures of the Green Lantern Corps, DC has a well-established galactic scene, full of feuding aliens, killer robots, space cops, and a giant wall made from dead gods that…
body: Some of that's a little too out there for a live-action TV show, but Lanterns still packs a great deal into its first season, including a reference to the planet-sized Green Lantern Mogo. Notably, it did remember to include the most important part of the entire Green Lantern mythos: Hal Jordan spends a lot of time unconscious.

Through sheer coincidence, the first episode of Lanterns came out a month after the 20-year anniversary of one of the internet comic book community's longest running gags: the Hal Jordan Head Injury Project. More surprisingly, due to the inexplicable immortality of both Flickr and Blogspot accounts, most of the HJHIP is still online today.

Put together by "Sleestak," who still blogs occasionally at Lady, That's My Skull, the HJHIP is a tongue-in-cheek tracker of the sheer number of times that Hal Jordan, in his nearly 70-year history as a character, has taken a shot to the dome.

The best/worst part of the HJHIP is that two of the greatest Hal Jordan skull cracks aren't currently in the archive. The best one that is, however, might be from a particularly wild Silver Age story.
points: HBO Max's Lanterns has made the cosmic side of the DC Universe more popular than it's been in a while.

articles.title: Resident Evil Dev Capcom Plans To Embrace AI In Game Development
articles.summary: A Capcom developer recently made some eyebrow-raising statements about integrating AI into RE Engine, the game engine Capcom uses to make games like Resident Evil Requiem, Pragmata, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword.
body: These surprising statements came from programmer Satoshi Ishida at Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026, a tech conference that the company holds to showcase developments on the RE Engine. Reported on first by GameBiz and translated by IGN, Ishida discussed the REX Project, which is meant to evolve RE Engine "for the next generation."

Many of these improvements aren't AI-related and simply focus on things like data formatting or memory management. That said, Ishida also made comments like "successfully integrating AI technology into development workflows has become an essential condition for streamlining future development," and "our goal is a future where we create games together with AI."

Those statements are certainly red flags if you don't want AI involved in game development, although the kind of AI Ishida refers to differs from generative AI used to create art or other game assets. As of March 2026, Capcom had told investors that it did not plan to use generative AI to create content for its games. Resident Evil Requiem was one of the games used in Nvidia DLSS 5's controversial reveal.

body: For example, a couple of The Simpsons voice actors have made headlines recently, which have gotten big reactions from fans. articles.title: Capcom plans to evolve RE Engine into an "AI-generation game engine"
articles.summary: Capcom wants to transform its in-house RE Engine into what it's calling an "AI-generation game engine".
body: As reported by gamebiz (via VGC ), programmer Satoshi Ishida outlined the plans at the "Capcom Open Conference RE:2026" event yesterday (2nd October), explaining that the changes were coming as part of an ongoing overhaul dubbed the REX Project.
RE Engine has been in development since 2014 and made its debut in Resident Evil 7 back in 2017. It's since been the engine behind the best part of 30 Capcom titles.

Ishida pointed to three challenges driving the REX Project – one, games have grown so large in scope and data volume that build and iteration times are slowing development down; two, RE Engine is now used by over 2,000 developers, including international staff and people coming from other engines, requiring better multilingual and accessibility support; and three, AI needs to be built into the development pipeline rather than bolted on.

That's why Capcom intends to bundle several new systems into the REX Project, including RE:Dox, which standardises data processing across formats, RE:UI, which speeds up development tools by separating appearance from state, and RE:Log, which swaps text-based logging for an ID-based system.
points: Capcom wants to transform its in-house RE Engine into what it's calling an "AI-generation game engine".

articles.title: Memory shortages set to persist into 2028, warns Micron CEO
articles.summary: Micron has warned that global RAM shortages show no sign of easing, telling investors on its earnings call that it has already sold most of next year's production.
body: As reported by The Register, CEO and chair Sanjay Mehrotra suggested customers should brace for prices well above what they paid in 2026, adding demand would keep outstripping supply through 2027 and into 2028, and calling the industry's supply-demand balance "only getting tighter".
The CEO also admitted that Micron does "not have line of sight to when supply and demand will return to balance".

As most of the capacity is booked for the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) needed for AI datacentres, the big three memory manufacturers - which includes Samsung - have very little dedicated to consumer-grade memory, which caused their prices to shoot up.

That has, in turn, pushed up the prices of pretty much every consumer electronic device that uses these chips, including game consoles like the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S and Switch 2 - all of which have gone up in price several times in some cases. Valve's Steam Machine also launched at a much higher price than Valve expected, and the company hinted it may even have to raise prices again.
points: Micron has warned that global RAM shortages show no sign of easing, telling investors on its earnings call that it has already sold most of next year's production.

articles.title: Deadlock's new hero Rat King has over 100 voice lines dedicated to throwing rats at you
articles.summary: Gaming's worst-kept secret Deadlock received a humongous update earlier this week, one that redecorated its entire town and added six new classes for players to sink their teeth into.
body: Rat King loves two things in life: rats, and throwing rats at his enemies. In fact, he enjoys rat tossing so much that he has more than 100 voice lines dedicated to his calling.

According to Deadlock voice line viewer (yes, that is a site that exists) Rat King entered the fray with a grand total of 1534 individual utterances, a similar number to most other Deadlock heroes. Of those lines, 126 of them are dedicated to his power "Rat Swarm", whereby Rat King unleashes a swarm of rodents from beneath his resplendent cape—which leap onto enemies and deal spirit damage over time.

Why so many voice lines for a single power? Well, I suppose the short answer is "because Valve can". But the longer answer is that, although some of the lines are generic power callouts (such as "I got a whole lotta rats, baby!") many of them refer to individual rats by name.

articles.title: "We felt that fans were getting a bit desensitised to the violence" Gears of War: E-Day devs made a "big investment" in gore, and weirdly, it works
articles.summary: Buoyed by some commendatory early reviews and fantastic initial player numbers, Gears of War: E-Day has found a solid audience a weekend before general release. And a large part of its appeal is the combat; I noted in my review I think it's the tightest Gears has ever been, augmented by some…
body: And it turns out there's a lot more intricate thought behind this eruption of violence than perhaps people realise, as I discovered in an interview with Coalition studio art director Aryan Hanbeck, brand director Nicole Fawcett, and creative director Matt Searcy.

"Think about getting a headshot, right, a really good headshot," says Hanbeck. "A lot of work goes into that moment, into what happens on the screen when you take a headshot. There's an audio component to that, too, as well as all the effects - how high the blood spurts go, how much mist we leave behind, what the body does afterwards… So, it's not just the weapon itself, it's what you see and hear when you do what it's supposed to do, or when you get up close and you melee with [your Lancer or Breechshot] or execute an enemy, which is really cool."
"And there's a big investment in gore in this game," adds Searcy. "That's a huge aspect of [what makes combat so satisfying]."

articles.title: Metro Redux's Next-Gen Update arrives this month as franchise passes 50 million sales
articles.summary: A free next-gen update is coming to Metro 2033 Redux and Metro Last Light Redux on 22nd October for PC (29th October for consoles).
body: The update comes as the Metro series passes 50 million copies sold worldwide, 16 years on from the original Metro 2033's release.

The studio stresses that the update "isn't a full remaster or remake", but "the original Metro Redux experience and aesthetic has been preserved" with the addition of 4K textures across all platforms, improved animations, higher-quality audio, and richer environmental detail, alongside a batch of community-requested bug fixes and quality-of-life changes.

On PlayStation 5, PS5 Pro, and Xbox Series X/S, the update adds native support with platform-specific extras, including PSSR on PS5 Pro, TSR upscaling and anti-aliasing on Xbox Series X, and spatial audio on Xbox platforms more broadly.

Console players will also be able to run the games at native 4K/60fps or upscaled 4K/120fps on compatible displays, with upgraded lighting, shadows and particle effects, DualSense Adaptive Triggers and Xbox Impulse Triggers, hardware tessellation and displacement, and power-saving modes on both platforms.

articles.title: 2026 is the year big brands have finally pushed gaming mouse technology forwards
articles.summary: Jacob got his hands on a gaming PC for the first time when he was about 12 years old. He swiftly realised the local PC repair store had ripped him off with his build and vowed never to let another soul build his rig again. With this vow, Jacob the hardware junkie was born.
body: This week I've been: trying out the X3 Superstrike and Sensei Pro gaming mice, as well as a new Logitech Hall effect keyboard.

What comes to mind when I say 'big brand competitive gaming mouse'? If you're anything like me, that particular Rorschach test will make you spit out the word 'expensive.' That response isn't wrong, either: just look at the big releases we've had this year.

There was the Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike: $180. The Razer Viper V4 Pro: $160. The SteelSeries Rival Pro and Sensei Pro: each $180. And there's an X3 Superstrike now, too, which is $200. These are some very expensive mice.

In previous years, I would have taken a dimmer view of this. Especially given the impressively competitive rodents you can pick up from niche Chinese brands these days. The $89 Mchose K7 V2 Ultra+, for example, is a Razer Viper V3/V4 Pro clone that performs very well and is plenty comfy.

articles.title: Love and Deepspace Devs Issue Warning to Players After Deadly Drink Recipes Go Viral
articles.summary: The official social media account for the popular RPG-dating sim Love and Deepspace issued a warning to players after announcing some fictional cocktails with potentially disastrous real-world consequences if actually consumed.
body: On September 28, Love and Deepspace revealed five ‘Shimmering Blend’ cocktail recipes as part of an in-game event, each themed around one of the game’s dashing romanceable characters. While they’re pretty to look at, you shouldn’t actually make some of these, as they include garnishes that are poisonous to humans.
For example, one of these drinks is made of pomegranate juice, with a garnish of cinnamon and datura. Another features sweet peach juice with a flame lily garnish and gelatin sheets.

There’s nothing wrong with peach and pomegranate juice, but these floral garnishes are making some players anxious that a fan might actually try to out the recipes themselves. Datura is a highly poisonous plant and is considered psychoactive; when consumed, it produces side effects like delirium, fever, tachychardia, and hallucinations.

Flame Lilies are also dangerous, as all parts of the plant contain a chemical called colchicine; while it’s used for medicinal purposes, it can be lethal, causing symptoms like fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and even hypovolemic shock, which causes the loss of lethal amounts of blood and bodily fluids.

articles.title: 007 First Light gets free DLC that will finally let you drive James Bond's Aston Martin properly
articles.summary: I thoroughly enjoyed 007: First Light when it launched back in May, but one area where I thought it fell short of delivering a fully-fledged James Bond experience was in its cars.
body: Most disappointing is the late game sequence involving an Aston Martin Valhalla, which also appears briefly in the most recent Bond film, No Time to Die. IO Interactive spends pretty much the entire game teasing the Valhalla, with the car gleaming alluringly on a pedestal every time you enter Q-Lab. But when Bond finally gets to sit in the driver's seat, it's essentially used for a short turret sequence and you don't get to drive anywhere.

Thankfully, this flaw has now been addressed—sort of. Earlier this week, IO Interactive released a free DLC pack for First Light. Titled 'Extended Operations' it adds a bunch of new modes and missions to the game, including one that finally lets you take the Valhalla out onto the road.

The mission is called Valhalla Protocol, and it's part of First Light's TacSim mode—which is a bit like Metal Gear Solid 's VR missions if they had a preposterous budget. Valhalla Protocol lets you cut about the mountains of Slovakia in Bond's heavily armed sports car, blowing up drones and other vehicles using its rockets and twin machine guns.

On October 2, Capcom held its own tech conference, called ‘Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026.’ One of the…
body: As reported by Japanese news outlet GameBiz, Ishida mentioned three major issues that Capcom is currently experiencing when it comes to game development: First, games are now so massive that simple processes have become extremely time-consuming; increased numbers of staff mean an engine is needed that’s easy for everyone to use; and finally, “successfully integrating AI technology into development workflows has become an essential condition for streamlining future development.”

GameBiz’s report confirmed that REX was created to help solve these problems by improving the efficiency of game development, game performance, tools, quality assurance, etc. Capcom felt that, rather than creating a brand-new engine from scratch, gradually adding these improvements over time is the best way to help evolve the RE Engine to the next generation.

We won’t get into the weeds of all the specific improvements included in the REX program, but Capcom is making at least some of them open-source for the purpose of training AI. Most interestingly, AI plays into Capcom’s larger, long-term goal of turning the RE Engine into an “AI-generation game engine” using its REX improvements.

points: The 2026 World Series has now passed its halfway mark, with Round 3 taking place in Singapore.
In the previous Round in Tokyo, reigning champion José Serrano dominated the race right up until the final lap, only to drop to 5th place due to a costly penalty.
This dramatic turn of events has significantly impacted the Points Ranking, in a race where the all the Spaniards were expected to hold the advantage.

videos.summary: Welcome back to Next-Gen Console Watch! This week Daemon, Ryan, and Max take a look at ex-PlayStation Worldwide Studios boss Shuhei Yoshida's recent comments about this current generation.
points: This week Daemon, Ryan, and Max take a look at ex-PlayStation Worldwide Studios boss Shuhei Yoshida's recent comments about this current generation.
Yoshida doesn't think gamers are interested in a PlayStation 6 or really any new generation of gaming hardware, and the PS5/Switch 2 generation should go for as long as possible.
While our wallets might appreciate, can PlayStation's business model go beyond the usual 5-7 year lifespan of gaming hardware?
And what about Microsoft, whose Xbox business has not been performing well in the last two generations?

body: Set in 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu and Ken Masters are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate, and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don’t, it’s GAME OVER!
